past_events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 11:45 doors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. 
 
 
 
 
    Reserve a spot
   
 
 
 
 
 
 PS…Class will be cancelled next week, Nov. 28th. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and Somerville resident. Since 2022, she spent two and a half years studying and teaching Hatha at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia before moving to Massachusetts.  She is currently teaching weekly Integral Yoga Hatha classes at the Lilypad and other spaces around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

past_events.description: Toad Revival Series — Saturdays, 4–7 PM  Every Saturday from 4 to 7, we rewind the clock and let the old sparks fly. The  Toad Revival Series  is our tribute to the bands that built this stage, note by note, night after night. It’s a laid-back, early evening show filled with familiar sounds, longtime favorites, and the spirit of a scene that never really faded—just waited for the right time to plug back in. These are the artists who gave Toad its heartbeat, returning for intimate, no-frills sets that remind us why we’re here. Think front-porch energy with barroom volume, old songs with new life, and a crowd that knows when to sing along. Come early. Stay as long as you like. This is Toad, the way it was—and still is.

past_events.title: A Special Night of Western Mass Hip-Hop
past_events.description:
$10 cover / 7pm doors / standing / all ages A Special Night of Western Mass Hip-Hop::: old school and new school underground hip-hop from the hills of Western Mass. Featuring Unagi, Dome Lettuce, DJ Toro, Bravo, Soma79, Hymn. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Unagi 
 
 
 Unagi is a Western Mass hip-hop pioneer, producer, rapper, and DJ, who started making music in the 90s with his crew Discs of Tron. A student of the old school, his music is full of dusty samples and boom bap drums, while his lyrical style is heavy on the storytelling, nostalgia, and good vibes. After many years in San Francisco he is back in the Bay State, collaborating with the next generation, putting out new records, and rocking an elaborate multimedia stage show. His latest album “Western Mass Hysteria” is out now. www.unagi442.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Dome Lettuce 
 
 
 Dome Lettuce is the primary musical alias of Gabriel Aviv, a 23 year old rapper, producer, DJ, and visual artist from Northampton Massachusetts. Since becoming active in 2019, he has been on a prolific run, releasing dozens of self produced albums, EPs, and singles. The near constant stream of new material combined with consistent live shows has earned him a dedicated following both locally and online, solidifying him as a unique fixture in the current underground. www.domelettuce.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Soma79 
 
 
 Soma79 is a hip-hop artist, designer, and storyteller from Hadley Mass, known for his innovative blend of boom-bap grit, earnest themes, and surreal visuals. He has been recording and doing shows for over 20 years, and has worked with iconic emcees like Kool Keith, Esoteric (of Czarface), Ras Kass, Copywrite, Elzhi, and many more. He recently released a new record called "Drinking Songs For Children."  www.soma79.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 DJ Toro Bravo 
 
 
 DJ Toro Bravo is a producer, engineer, DJ, and multi-instrumentalist. Based in Greenfield Mass, he has toured the world with a wide variety of artists across all genres.

past_events.title: Chuck Clough
past_events.description:
A Boston area singer/guitarist, Chuck primarily performs solo but also plays out with his band, The Butler Frogs. He has opened for touring bands America, The Wallflowers, and The Gin Blossoms. In 2020, The Butler Frogs released their sole EP, Last Call For Opinions.

He was also a founding member of Northern Point (2005-2010), an acoustic trio from the NY/NJ area that released three albums (November, Northern Point: Live at St. James' Gate, and After The Frost). 

In 2016, Chuck founded and hosted (with musician Ronnie Hirschberg) the award-winning podcast Above The Basement - Boston Music and Conversation, which won a 202o Boston Music Award for Podcast/Radio Show of the Year.  After 200 episodes, Chuck shuttered the podcast and set out on his solo musical endeavor. 

 He currently performs in New England and is always on the lookout for the lost songs that have influenced him over the years.

Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
past_events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

past_events.title: Luis Reyes Quintet / The Quantum Collective
past_events.description:
$15 admission / $10 for students / 10pm doors / 10:30 show / seated Luis Reyes Quintet 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Led by saxophonist and composer Luis Reyes, the quintet is an ensemble of musicians from Boston's vibrant jazz community. Performing original compositions that draw from a wide range of influences, from hard bop to modern jazz, the group embraces the depth of the jazz tradition while exploring the possibilities of contemporary improvisation. With a sound that is both rooted in tradition and forward-looking, the quintet reflects the diverse and evolving spirit of modern jazz. @luisreyes_saxophone The Quantum Collective  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A brainchild of local trumpeter Matt Kelly, The Quantum Collective bursts with energy and vitality, trying to capture the urgency of this moment through the lens of Black American Music. The quintet eschews the electronic experimentation of sister band Quantum Moon for a more grounded and tactile approach. Taking cues from visionary musicians and activists like Max Roach, Gil Scott-Heron, and Sons of Kemet, The Quantum Collective leans into the fact that making music is an inherently political act and every note can be a barb in the side of an authoritarian institution while also capturing the joy and resilience in our hearts. So come dig deep and let loose in joyful rage and beautiful sadness. @mattkellytrumpet mattkellytrumpet.com

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer.  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow.
